key_insight: ARISE uses authentic-content reference geometry to learn emerging multimodal forgery attacks while reducing forgetting of earlier attacks.
engineering_relevance: The method targets continually updated multimodal forensic systems, not solid mechanics or constitutive modeling.
method: Fit a real-only Gaussian mixture model to projected authentic replay representations.
Use GRASP to preserve historically stable representation directions while allowing adaptation elsewhere.
Use VAR to emphasize vulnerable historical stages based on training-time replay statistics, without adding inference modules.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved historical retention and final average performance across three Fable-Bench attack-evolution protocols and multiple detector architectures, but provides no numerical results.
watch_item: Effectiveness may depend on how well the replay buffer and Gaussian mixture capture authentic-content diversity.
paper_title: ARISE: Authentic Reference-Informed Stability Enhancement for Continual Multimodal Forgery Detection
